headline: Drugmaker GSK has widened its work with AI company Chai Discovery after its own lab tests of Chai's designs went well.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a notable pharma-AI deal, but the results are the companies' own statements and terms are not given.
importance_line: It signals a large drugmaker putting more trust in AI-designed molecules after wet-lab testing, which could speed early drug discovery for patients, but the evidence is the two companies' own account and no data or financial terms were published in the report.
summary: Contract Pharma reports, citing Chai Discovery's announcement, that drugmaker GSK has begun a broader collaboration with Chai, an AI company building design software for molecules, after GSK tested Chai's designs in its own laboratory. Chai says its models, run without target-specific training, produced binders (molecules that attach to a disease target) for all the GSK targets tested, and GSK's Christopher Austin said the designs showed "strong binding affinities"; both statements are the companies' own and the report gives no financial terms.
notes: Pool item is Fierce Biotech (https://www.fiercebiotech.com/biotech/gsk-drinks-chai-discoverys-ai-models-after-wet-lab-validation), blocked 403; url here is Contract Pharma where text was read. Original is Chai's Business Wire release (also blocked).
